notes.title: Nominate Clash for Story Rich in the Steam Awards!
notes.content:
Tis that time of the year, where people are ready to get past all this Fall nonsense and jump into Christmas.  But never mind that, we are here to talk Steam Awards and Autumn Sales!

I humbly ask that you consider nominating [i]Clash: Robot Detective - Complete Edition[/i] for the Story Rich award.  I'm just one lady so I can't really bribe you or anything about this, and heck I sincerely doubt I'll even get in considering I released the same year as [i]South Scrimshaw[/i] (oh and all those big name games like BG3 I guess), but even just one person finding my little story grand enough to nominate it for an award would mean so much.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/11f4284fba01b87b724963f58f34e9e2c36ffe81.png[/img]

And if you haven't had a chance to actually play the game and judge the story for yourself, it's on sale in the Autumn Sale this week for 50% off!  Or at least it should be, as of posting this I don't think the change has actually taken place, but keep checking back and do consider grabbing a copy if you haven't yet because you will fund my classroom supplies I need so many tissue boxes and pencils like you have no idea man.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/b9967601377ea3b4396ff16ce9ef7c078038f75a.png[/img]

To wrap it up, I am very grateful for all the support Clash and I have gotten throughout the years.  When I wrote the very first version back in 2021, I did not think I'd have anyone reading it at all.  But I have gotten some lovely messages and fanart since then, as well as opportunities for growth that I really never thought I'd get (more details on that cryptic comment as they arrive).  I've even been able to take what I've learned from the experience and use it to teach and encourage others with writing as well; that's really the best part, honestly.  It's not about money or awards (although to be quite frank, those are very nice to have), its about the smiles.

So from the bottom of Clash's heart of gold:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/0f38523e99dfab8086a86a30adef1d80bd072b07.png[/img]

tldr, nominate and/or purchase Clash this week.  :-)

notes.title: Quick Announcement/Update about the eBook DLC...
notes.content:
So the first big piece of news: yes, I'm working on it.  For the first draft, I'm just porting all the lines over into a Word document and then reformatting them into something more bookish.  From there, its just going to be revising and making it read like PROPER LITERATURE.  Okay, maybe not "proper" on the lines of Sherlock Holmes or something.  But more proper than it currently is.

But as I'm going through, I'm noticing a lot of lines that aren't as clear as when I first wrote the visual novel.  Which is a normal process, I've learned.  What reads great before doesn't read so well when you check on it months or years later.  But the great thing about visual novels is that you can update them much easier than you can a published book.  So while I am working on the novelization, I'm also revising the game.

So eventually, this game is going to get not only an eBook for DLC but it will get what I assume will be a fairly big update.  Basically revising scenes from good to better.  I'll come up with a kicky name for this update later.

No idea when either will release just yet, so stay tuned.  :-)

(Also if you haven't checked out the sequel's demo yet, its still up and its still in Next Fest.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2323650/Clash_Blue_Mirage/

So there you go, there's that.)

notes.title: Novelization DLC Coming Soonish!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/983ca82ae1344eb78a22837edf83e9c3792e3447.png[/img]

I will let you in on a secret: when I was younger, I liked to write novelizations.  No idea why.  But I liked writing them for my favorite movies and tv show episodes and would share them with my friends and family (cute or cringe?  You decide!).  As I got older I stopped, but there was still a tiny part of me that missed writing them.

So now that I am an adult and can make my own life choices, I have decided to novelize Clash.  And it will be released as DLC, right here on Steam*!

*also on itch.io, but we're not here to talk about itch.io, we're here to talk about Steam.

The book is going to follow the plot of the game, but with some specific choices (like perpetrator, dealing with Jasper, and the name/gender of the player character).  If they aren't the choices you made, that is okay; this novelization isn't necessarily THE route.  It will have both the main game and the bonus story, as well as some interludes from Clash's past.

Now, I am taking my time with this.  I'm actually writing out the first draft by hand, which will then be transferred to a word document for editing (I learned long ago to do writing projects this way; this way, there's a hard copy to refer to if the digital is lost...and plus its just plain fun to write out stories the old-fashioned way).  Then its editing, editing, editing.  

So I honestly have no idea how long the process will take or when the ebook will be available.

Just that it WILL be available at some point.  I'm bound and determined to make it so.  So stay tuned!

(And yes, Clash: Blue Mirage is still being made.  Demo should be here mid-to-late February, depending on how early I can launch the game page once I've got it designed.)

notes.title: Thank You!!!
notes.content:
Its about a week since the game went live on Steam, and boy what a week its been!  Not counting that little hiccup with the Steam achievements (which was caught and fixed so quickly only because you guys were so helpful and patient with me!), this launch week has gone smoothly.  The only basis of comparison I have for 'success' is the last time I tried a Steam release; looking at the stats, that game got in half a year (in views, clicks, and purchases) what Clash got in one week.  So there's definitely been improvement.  xD

In all seriousness, coming back to Steam was a nervewracking decision.  If I falied again, it would suck. 
 But because of the support of you - the player! - it has been a success.

So a hundred and a thousand times: [b]thank you!!![/b]

So, what next?  Well...I still need to go back and get all the achievements, since I deleted them all whenever I tested them.  Speaking of achievements, here's some fun stats based on the first week of them:
[list]
[*]You lot are a friendly bunch, seeing as how that path was the most common
[*]You lot also chose to take the path of the 'good cop' more than the path of the 'bad cop'
[*]Its about equal how you all dealt with Jasper; punchin' or flirtin', it was all good
[*]40% wanted Clash to spend the night with them ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°)
[*]20% got Julian to let Clash stick around for his interrogation
[*]Only 10% of you had to step in and help Clash interrogate the waiter
[*]And there's a ten-percent difference between people who started the game and people who actually met Clash, not sure what's going on there but okay
[/list]

I also will be keeping an eye on discussions, reviews, and/or curator posts to see what people think of Clash (so if you've enjoyed your time with the game, please consider leaving a review!).  And getting my rear end into gear so that I can get Clash: Blue Mirage's demo ready for Steam.  Yes, the sequel is already coming.  I don't know when exactly, but it is coming.  

Again, [b]thank you[/b] to everyone who has made Clash a success on Steam!  I hope you continue to enjoy the game!

notes.title: Clash: Robot Detective - Odds & Ends
notes.content:
The third Hype Update is here on a fantastically chilly Christmas Eve.  So a merry happy to all of you out there, I hope you are staying warm!  Here's a picture from the sequel of Clash wearing a scarf to encourage your warmness.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/7078266c6445654fbf2f9c4a1a444c0ec47e436b.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/14ad511b48e6c30b1741de553fcb0a913e8cabd4.png[/img][/url]

(btw, consider this the official Steam announcement that Clash 2 is coming soon, but let's focus on the Clash 1 port for now).

Two updates ago, I talked about the main campaign and what makes it special.  Last update, I talked about the bonus episode / trivia scene and what makes it special.  This update, let's talk nitty gritty.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/a2faf5f807894e8f00ee2c6618fa8a61abb46acd.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/791af509bc7bab35d967c558f2c8da542c6d99e1.png[/img][/url]

The sprite editing process was very obnoxious.  I believe I mentioned this before, but it bears repeating: I cannot draw.  My art style stalled out at first grade.  I could develop a style, but that would take time and/or money for art classes; I don't have either.  Also can't afford artists.  So I had to find a way around my inability to draw; hence, the weird collage visuals.  That actually worked out quite nice, its a very distinct look and it has grown on me.

So when I decided to "remaster" the game, I went back and touched up the sprites.  As seen on the image above, the sprites originally had a bunch of pixels around them due to me choosing to erase all unneeded bits myself instead of doing something easier.  Sad part is, the change can barely be noticed; when I went back and tested it, there was little to no visible difference.  Probably could have saved time and not even done it, no one would have been wiser.

But I know they're fixed up, and that's the important part. :-)

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/219552497aeda66c2ae5e9ba715977b4d3b7a868.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/2baef2cd0454ee9efbb6c8400703c7cc2d92ce4f.png[/img][/url]

I also fixed up dialogue bits and added more achievements.  Editing dialogue - that's something that should have been done a long time ago.  Revising is the key to success and I should do it more.  That's about all I have to say about editing dialogue.

Achievements are fun.  They should sync up to Steam, as well (and if they don't, do let me know; I can't actually test them until after the game releases).  I did not add an in-game pop-up for whenever an achievement is collected; if there was an in-game pop-up alongside the Steam pop-up, I thought that would get annoying.  And the Achievement screen is a list because I like lists, they are nice and organized.  It may not be how other visual novels handle their Achievements screens, but it is how I handle mine.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/20680540229c431a5fea07891b43ec0cd12a6e5b.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/c55bcf7d035fee4967b92eafa65d559733af2311.png[/img][/url]

I hope that is the main takeaway from this update: that I'm doing this not because I'm trying to make some focus-tested perfect VN, but because this is the game I wanted to make the way I wanted to make it.  And I certainly hope that you - the Steam gamer reading this! - are sufficiently convinced that you want to play the game I made the way I wanted to make it.  Even if these posts have been weird and awkward.  I'm still learning.

That's the end of the three pre-release hype updates!  I'll have one more next week just for the heck of it.  Then that will be the last time you hear from me before the game launches on [i]January 2nd, 2023[/i]!

So I will see you here next week, same Clash time!  Same Clash channel!  [spoiler]Please tell me that reference has not been lost to time.[/spoiler]

notes.title: Clash: Robot Detective - Baristas and Bonuses
notes.content:
Welcome back to the biweekly hype updates for [i]Clash: Robot Detective - Complete Edition[/i]'s Steam release!  Last week, I talked a bit about the main game: where it came from, why I like it, etc.  Today, I want to look at the extra bits that were added specifically for the Complete Edition: the behind-the-scenes trivia and the post-main-story chapter, [i]Steel Barista[/i].

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/fda560381d8b90b8d86f02b3e9460402aad9bf6c.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/eb87e439d88eaca77f5d883f92edbf53f799aea2.png[/img][/url]

Yes, behind-the-scenes trivia is awfully self-indulgent.  But I hadn't planned on it.  I was trying to figure out how to code the "Play Bonus Story" menu button to show up only after the Main Story was completed.  That code consistently crashed the game.  So, biting back the frustration, I tried a different approach.  What if the button was available, but just gave the player a reminder to finish the Main Story if they hadn't?  That worked great: click Bonus Story, a black screen would pop up saying "You can't play this yet" and then boot the player back to the main menu.  Then I though, "Wouldn't it be funny if Clash popped up and yelled at the player for trying to play the chapters out of order?"  So i slapped one of the Clash sprites in there.  At that point, I figured it would actually be kind of neat if there was a whole secret scene for players to find.  Didn't want it to be story-related, in case the player missed it.  So the trivia thing just kind of fell into my lap: it was easy to write out, it was fun to ramble about the making of the game, and it was just a neat idea.  Then I felt bad about making it potentially missable, so I added some code that gave people who had finished the main story the option to pick between the trivia and the bonus story.  Et voila!  A nice chunk of bonuses dedicated to trivia, which had never been in my plans to begin with!

This was a very long-winded way to say "I pulled out of my rear end."

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/b26ff6611ccedd1267fc8c5355136ebff6647198.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/4b096f21f755d5144a8b9ad4e75cc340911f3bc5.png[/img][/url]

The bonus story is based on a couple of different interactive fiction pieces I wrote for a couple of different game jams.  Both did very well in their respective competitions, and both added to Clash's character in ways I liked.  My main idea with updating Clash to the Complete Edition was to bring these stories back to the main canon.  This meant refining and editing them both, as well as adding visuals.  Neither of the interactive fiction games had these.

The bulk of the story is patterned after [i]Steel Barista[/i] (and is named as such).  It was submitted to a jam with the theme of 'cliffhanger.'  So it had to end in one.  That theme made me think of mysteries and noir detectives.  Which, of course, I already had one: Clash!  I wanted it to be more tightly-paced and lower-scaled than [i]Robot Detective[/i], so instead of running around a high-tech cruise ship Clash would just be running around a city.  I had trouble figuring out the story from there until I got to reminiscing about high school.  In 11th grade, we read a very specific Agatha Christie book (which, if I tell you the name of it right now, will spoil the whole story).  When I read that book's twist, I was both amazed and furious; I almost threw the book down the hall in sheer emotion!  Then I thought, "I wonder if I could pull that twist off?  Let's experiment and see!"  

I also wanted to give Clash a conundrum.  He is a nice robot man.  TOO nice.  Dangerously close to Gary Stu levels of nice.  What if he had to make a tough decision?  A decision between doing the right thing or doing what he wanted to do?  A choice between reason and passion?  Could he do that?  WOULD he do that?  That was my cliffhanger: no one will know what Clash chose.  [i]I[/i] don't even know what he would have chosen.  I refuse to say what his canonical choice was.  That's up to you to decide.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/9e89eac47a0c9919f26b1cf651f0f2e9b081e32e.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/620121422747a386bc181558f23a8461318861ee.png[/img][/url]

The epilogue for the story is a heavily-edited [i]Curious Set[/i], which due to the content of that story NEEDED to be heavily edited.  In this story, Clash and [strike]my self-insert character[/strike] Victoria "work together" so that Clash can learn more about himself and the passionate side of humanity.  It goes off the rails from there.

So the epilogue stays firmly on the rails (if you want to read the off-the-rails version, you will need to be an adult and you will need to go to itchio and find it yourself).  But that whole "a robot not built for romantic endeavors will not understand them, but wants to know because he needs to understand why humans let their romantic endeavors lead them to crimes of passion" angle was one that I wanted to keep in the canon.  It sums up a part of Clash's character: he constantly wants to learn.  He wants to understand so that he can do his job better and help others more efficiently.  And maybe he gets a little too attached to the people in his life.  It happens.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/20680540229c431a5fea07891b43ec0cd12a6e5b.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/c55bcf7d035fee4967b92eafa65d559733af2311.png[/img][/url]

And those are the bonuses!  Two weeks from now will be the third hype update.  In it, I will talk about some of the smaller details that make Clash Complete worth looking in to.  Also, general Christmas well-wishing.  Because I'm that kind of person.  :-)

notes.title: Clash: Robot Detective - A Quick Rundown
notes.content:
Hello, all you prospective detective assistants!  My name is Sci and I am the weird lady behind Drone Garden Studios.  I've been writing visual novels (and RPGs and narrative adventures, but mostly visual novels) for a couple of years now.  I started as a way to keep myself busy/working during certain lockdown periods and just...sort of...didn't stop.  It's a very fun side hustle.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/98819b9b0a87b8b2be4a74b15e48c34d92f42df1.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/e20bbc0139ee952f3d82391a5cfa5d6d56239730.png[/img][/url]

[i]Clash: Robot Detective[/i] was first released in September 2021.  It's a mystery/sci-fi visual novel about a robot detective who hires an unwary human (that's you, the player!) to help him solve a mystery onboard a high-tech cruise ship.  If it sounds like a strange premise, that is because it was inspired by a couple of different dreams I had that same year that would not leave my head.

The game was a success on itch.io!  Or at least, a success by my margin.  Good reviews from users, nice rankings in game jams, things like that.  But most importantly, [i]I[/i] was happy with it.  Clash ended up being my favorite character I'd created.  I wrote a couple of interactive fiction mini-sequels just to keep working on his characterization.  I ended up expanding on the original game by adding those sequels into it, as well as other assorted goodies (hence, the "Complete Edition" subtitle).  And again, people seemed to like him as much as I did.

I wanted to share him with a wider audience.  Which meant...*gulp*...coming to Steam.  No matter how intimidating that was.

And now we're here.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/e3560ac359e8fb398eeb37ffe805d5cdae9f81f6.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/d9c7e3f8d08c5d6726f8e2b495ebcbf46e7ef7e4.png[/img][/url]

A big theme (for lack of a better term) of [i]Clash[/i] is player choice.  Taking inspiration from RPG speech checks, the player can affect the flow of the story by building up and testing their stats.  These stats affect two big plot twists: who the culprit is and what kind of detective Clash becomes.  You can check on these stats at any time by clicking the "Personality Traits" button, which was a feature added simply because I like being able to look at my stats.

This can end up creating a strange turn of events.  During a testing playthrough of mine, everything was pointing towards (SPOILER CHARACTER 1) being the culprit.  But halfway through, I decided to try building different stats...which led to the reveal that (SPOILER CHARACTER 2) had done it the whole time!  Also, Clash yelled at me due to the other set of stats I had built up.  :-(  But still, it created an interesting way to have a mystery unfold.  

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/46845b0460f219da48325fbf68a19162cd4f1f40.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43223122/9866461262d51b29a5b7655f01ebf39d86d48d01.png[/img][/url]

Something else I wanted to explore was robotic sentience.  Yes, its cliche.  But I love stories where a robot gains self-awareness.  Especially when the robot chooses to use that self-awareness to help rather than harm.  And Clash is still learning.  He's trying to figure out how life works.  He wants to help but can't figure out what the (censor) everyone's problem is.  He's tired and confused, but he refuses to give up.  He's sarcastic, but he has a heart of gold.  Possibly literally.

Even though he is not the playable character, he's the main character.  And I wanted to create a main character that people could root for.  And I think I succeeded.  [spoiler]Maybe too well, because I have it on good authority that some people want to kiss him.  Okay, but I saw him first.[/spoiler]
